## Highlights

- [Image generation](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/admin/governance/content-models#let-agents-generate-images) follows each image model's own limits. Tale reads what every OpenRouter image model accepts from OpenRouter's image model listing and asks a model for the closest shape it draws: Recraft's models draw no 3:2, so a landscape is 4:3 there, where every such request failed before. A request with more reference images than the model takes, or an edit model's request without a picture to start from, is refused before anything is billed, and the agent is told why. Vector models, which return SVG files that Tale does not store, are no longer offered, and the Seedream 5.0 models, which OpenRouter lists without a context window, now are ([#5057](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/5057)).
- **Automatic** image model selection no longer recommends GPT Image 1, which OpenAI shut down on October 23, 2026. It tries Gemini 2.5 Flash Image, GPT Image 2.5 Flare (the successor OpenAI names), GPT Image 1 Mini until OpenAI shuts it down on December 1, 2026, then FLUX.2 Pro. The OpenAI provider's catalog lists GPT Image 2.5 Flare, GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst and GPT Image 2 in place of GPT Image 1 ([#5057](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/5057)).
- [Start an image from a picture you attach in chat](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/chat/files-and-skills): asking to "turn the attached photo into a watercolor" now hands the photo to the image model. Before, the assistant saw the picture but not the file it came from, so it could not pass it on ([#5057](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/5057)).
- Through OpenRouter, a GPT image model is asked for `medium` quality, as Tale already asked OpenAI directly, so its price per image no longer depends on the quality the provider picks: on OpenRouter's default, GPT Image 1 Mini cost about four times its `medium` price ([#5057](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/5057)).

## Upgrade notes

- No migration runs, and the API contract stays at `3.49.0`.
- An organization whose image generation is on **Automatic** and reaches only OpenAI moves from GPT Image 1 Mini to GPT Image 2.5 Flare. OpenAI prices GPT Image 2.5 Flare's image output at USD 30 per million tokens, where GPT Image 1 Mini's is USD 8; pin GPT Image 1 Mini under **Settings › Governance › Models** to keep it until December 1, 2026.
- A pin on `gpt-image-1` through the OpenAI provider, or on a vector model, now shows as unavailable on the Models page, and agents get no image tool until an administrator chooses another model or **Automatic**. OpenRouter still lists `openai/gpt-image-1` and `openai/gpt-5-image`, and both fail at OpenAI: choose another model if you pinned one of them. A pinned edit model keeps working for requests that start from a picture.
- With an OpenRouter credential, the backend also reads `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/images/models`, a public listing that needs no key, with the catalog listings it already reads from `openrouter.ai`. An egress rule that admits `openrouter.ai` covers it; when the listing cannot be reached, image requests keep the facts last read, or Tale's previous defaults.
